subject: Civil Engineering
title: Pedestrian Infrastructure
description: Learn Pedestrian Infrastructure in one minute.

hook.text: A pedestrian is hit every seven minutes in the United States. Streets prioritize cars.

buildup.text: Sidewalks, crosswalks, and pedestrian signals form the basic walking infrastructure.

discovery.text: Curb ramps and tactile paving make streets accessible to wheelchair users and the blind.

twist.text: Leading pedestrian intervals give walkers a head start before cars get a green light.

climax.text: Pedestrian plazas in New York's Times Square replaced car lanes with chairs and tables.

punchline.text: Every trip starts and ends on foot. Design for that first step.

quiz.question: What is a leading pedestrian interval?
options: A longer green light phase for vehicles to clear the intersection
A head start for pedestrians to enter the crosswalk before vehicles get a green signal
A countdown timer showing pedestrians how long until the light changes
